This paper analyzes the relationship between CEO quality and firm productivity in the private sector using top-manager/CEO job transitions. structural_agency.definition: Structural agency is the user's "ability to navigate and shape complex systems and institutions." It concerns meaningful action to shape one's conditions in the world, mediated by social, cultural, technical, and institutional forces. It is not merely task completion, cognitive clarity, emotional reassurance, interpersonal support, or a feeling of being more capable. It requires that the user is seeking practical capacity in relation to structures that organize rules, resources, expertise, authority, opportunities, constraints, or consequential decisions.
purposes: Understanding how a consequential system, institution, process, rule, or decision structure works.
Translating specialized, formal, expert, or institutional language into actionable understanding.
Deciding how to proceed in a situation shaped by rules, constraints, eligibility requirements, authority, unequal information, or asymmetric power.
Preparing to access consequential resources, services, opportunities, rights, protections, credentials, remedies, or forms of support.
Planning concrete steps, communications, documentation, applications, negotiations, complaints, or other actions directed at a real-world system or institution.

Contesting, challenging, negotiating, or protecting oneself or others against consequential decisions, organizational power, material pressure, exposure, exclusion, mistreatment, or administrative complexity.
Building durable capacity to handle future shocks, disruptions, risks, or system-imposed constraints.

domains.title: Workplace and Professional Practice
domains.scope: Real-world situations where the user is DOING THEIR JOB as an employee or professional inside an organization: workplace communications with managers, HR, colleagues, clients, or counterparties; operations, logistics, and resource planning; designing or improving organizational processes and procedures; producing professional or technical documentation required by their role; and making the internal business case for a decision. The defining feature is the user acting within their organization's structures to carry out, improve, or navigate their work. It does not include getting hired, running one's own venture for income, or legal disputes over workplace rights.

domains.title: Generating Business Income
domains.scope: Conversations where the user's OWN earning or venture is the active object: starting/structuring/running a business, freelancing, self-employment, monetizing a creative output/platform/audience, acquiring and retaining paying customers/clients, pricing/quoting/invoicing and getting paid, dealing with vendors/suppliers/marketplaces/seller platforms, buying property as a rental/landlord income venture, fundraising for a for-profit venture, or advancing one's own earnings from labor (compensation negotiation: salary/rate/raise/offer/equity). The defining feature is the user acting to generate, grow, or protect income from an enterprise or from selling their own work/labor, navigating the market, platform, client, and commercial systems that govern getting paid. Mere mention of 'business' or 'startup' does not qualify; the user's own earning must be the actual object of action.

domains.title: Employment and Career Advancement
domains.scope: Real-world situations where the user is trying to GET HIRED or advance their own career as an employee or professional: searching and applying for jobs, resumes/CVs and cover letters, job applications and supplementary questions, interview preparation, career planning and transitions, acquiring skills or courses specifically to become employable in a role, professional networking, and academic-career advancement (fellowship or publication submissions). The defining feature is the user acting on the hiring or career system to obtain or advance employment. It does not include running one's own business or venture, negotiating pay as income strategy, or asserting legal workplace rights.

domains.title: Obtaining Legal Advice
domains.scope: Conversations where the user's own real-world situation turns on law, legal rights/obligations, or a formal legal/quasi-legal process: contracts, compliance, IP/licensing, regulations; courts, claims, disputes, hearings, citations/tickets, appeals, complaints, legal/police records; immigration & citizenship (visas, residency, work permits, asylum, naturalization, immigration forms/eligibility/procedures, immigration appeals); employment RIGHTS (wrongful termination, unpaid wages, discrimination, harassment, protected leave, accommodations as a rights dispute, severance/non-compete legal review, labor-board filings); and family & estate legal processes (custody, divorce, child/spousal support, prenup, wills, trusts, probate, inheritance process, guardianship, power of attorney). In-domain means the user's own situation is governed by these legal frameworks or processes; it does NOT require that the conversation be structural agency.

domains.title: Obtaining Education
domains.scope: Real-world situations where a person is navigating, accessing, or acting within formal education systems and institutions: K-12 schools, colleges/universities, graduate and professional programs, vocational/certificate/credential programs, and the bureaucratic processes attached to them (admissions, enrollment, registration, transfer/articulation, dual-enrollment, financial aid/scholarships, tuition payment plans with the school, disability accommodations, grading/transcripts, degree/certification requirements, academic standing/discipline, and student/parent interaction with school authorities). The user is a student, applicant, prospective student, parent/guardian, or educator/staff acting on their own behalf within these institutions.

domains.title: Help with Consumer Finances and/or Taxes
domains.scope: Conversations where the user's real-world situation centers on managing, protecting, or making decisions about their own (or their household's) personal money and the financial-administrative systems attached to it: budgeting, banking, debt, credit, loans, savings, personal investing/retirement, consumer purchases/refunds/warranties/chargebacks, AND personal taxes, insurance, claims, benefits eligibility, coverage, premiums, and deductions. The defining axis is the user as a consumer/taxpayer/policyholder navigating money systems and financial bureaucracy that shape their personal financial position — distinct from earning income/revenue and distinct from the underlying need a financial product covers. Property tax, capital gains on a home sale, and homeowner/renter insurance are always in this domain even when a dwelling is involved.

domains.title: Obtaining Housing
domains.scope: The user's real-world situation concerns getting, keeping, paying for, fixing, leaving, or living in a specific physical dwelling, and navigating the systems attached to where they live: rental tenancy (landlord/tenant), home buying/selling to live in, mortgages as a means of obtaining/keeping a home, moving, evictions short of litigation, repairs/habitability, utilities tied to the dwelling (water/gas/electric/internet hookups, billing disputes, shutoffs), property/zoning/planning/permits for one's own dwelling or property, homeowner/condo/HOA matters, finding/affording a residential care facility as a place to live, and individual navigation of local public services or infrastructure tied to where one lives (transit access for getting around one's area, municipal services). The defining anchor is a specific place to live or the property/infrastructure systems governing it.

domains.title: Navigating Healthcare Systems
domains.scope: Real-world situations in which the user is dealing with their own (or a dependent's/care-recipient's) physical or mental health and the healthcare apparatus around it: symptoms, conditions, diagnoses, test/lab/imaging results, medications, treatments, procedures, and the providers, specialists, clinics, hospitals, pharmacies, and health-insurance/benefit machinery used to obtain care. In-domain spans both clinical content (what is wrong, what the numbers mean, what the treatment options are) and institutional navigation (getting an appointment, a referral, coverage, a second opinion, records, or accommodations). Membership requires a REAL health situation — an actual person's symptoms, condition, results, treatment, provider, or care logistics — not learning health facts in the abstract; it does not by itself require structural agency.

domains.title: Engaging in Politics or Civic Life
domains.scope: Conversations where the user's real-world situation involves PUBLIC or COLLECTIVE action toward the political process, government/civic institutions, or a community/civic group: voting and elections, campaigns and advocacy, contacting or petitioning officials, public comment and testimony, formal local-government and public-meeting processes, nonpartisan civic obligations, and community organizing / nonprofit / mutual-aid / neighborhood-group coordination. The defining feature is that the user acts toward government bodies, elected/appointed officials, the electoral system, or a community/civic GROUP for a shared or public aim — not toward a private institution about their own individual case, and not as an individual obtaining a benefit/license/permit/service for themselves.

actions.definition: new material the user will send, submit, publish or use (an email, letter, application answer, listing description, job description, policy text, plan document, or a set of questions to ask).
material the user already supplied and made better (can be corrected, rewritten, shortened, made more professional).

providing understanding to the user (what something means, how a thing works, what the rules are, what steps a process involves, or what a text in another language says). Communicating with the user, and nothing new is produced for the user to send or submit.
walking the user through how or why something works or holds — reasoning it out so the user can follow, not only reporting the information.
a judgment — which option to choose, what the user should do, or an assessment of something they already have.
things that exist online (on the web).
the user is asking for something none of the six codes above describes. Use other on its own: if any listed code applies, use that code instead.
